page: Google Cloud Platform a3-ultragpu-8g-nolssd is an accelerator-optimized server designed for high-density GPU workloads. It features eight NVIDIA H200 GPUs from the Hopper family, providing a total of 1123 GB of VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with 224 vCPUs and 112 physical cores running at 2.1 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 2952.0 GB of system memory, yielding 13.18 GB of RAM per core.

A key architectural tradeoff of this specific configuration is the complete absence of local SSD storage, as local storage size is designated as none. This requires users to rely on network-attached storage solutions for data persistence and scratch space. The system does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier performance across multiple domains. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng, PassMark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all rank in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also achieve top-tier status, alongside Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput. However, single-core performance metrics, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core scores, fall into the average category. For LLM inference, text generation using a medium 7B model registers strong performance, while a large 70B model falls into the average tier.

Given the massive GPU memory capacity and high-density compute resources, this server is optimized for large-scale AI training, deep learning, and complex data science jobs. The qualitative cost efficiency of this server is defined by its high resource density, combining massive GPU acceleration with substantial system memory, though the lack of local storage requires careful architectural planning for data-heavy pipelines.
